title: Magnetism and Electrical Conduction in Lightly-Doped Single-Layer High-$T_c$ Cuprate $\mathrm{La}_2\mathrm{CuO}_{4+δ}$
authors: Kota Miyakoshi, Yuya Kinugawa, Shusei Mizuta, Yoshihiko Ihara, Hiroyuki K. Yoshida, Tohru Kurosawa, Yasunori Toda, Naoki Momono, Migaku Oda
abstract: The temperature dependences of magnetization and electrical resistivity as well as their magnetic field dependences have been examined in lightly-doped single-layer cuprate $\mathrm{La}_2\mathrm{CuO}_{4+δ}$ (LCO, hole-doping level $p \, (2δ) \cong 0.03$) single crystals, in comparison with those in the extremely low doping region of $p \lesssim 0.015$ to uncover the intrinsic magnetism and electrical conduction of the $\mathrm{Cu\text{-}O}$ plane that exhibits both antiferromagnetic (AF) and superconducting (SC) orders simultaneously. In $p \cong 0.03$ SC LCO, the sub-lattice moments on $\mathrm{Cu}$ sites and their AF couplings are only $\sim 15\,\%$ smaller than those of the Mott-insulator parent material, suggesting that the localization of $\mathrm{Cu}$ $3d$ electrons remains very strong. Furthermore, we report that in the SC LCO, two-dimensional AF spin correlations develop rapidly from $T^* \cong 280\text{ K}$ towards Néel temperature $T_{\mathrm{N}} = 266\text{ K}$, where the out-of-plane resistivity starts to decrease largely. This might be responsible for the AF ordering at such a high temperature in the SC single-layer cuprate with $p \cong 0.03$.
summary: This paper investigates the interplay between antiferromagnetism and superconductivity in lightly-doped single-layer cuprates. By measuring magnetization and resistivity, the authors argue that superconductivity is intrinsically linked to the robust, strongly correlated antiferromagnetic background of the $\mathrm{Cu-O}$ planes. The findings highlight the coexistence of these two orders in the superconducting state.
main_problem: To uncover the intrinsic magnetism and electrical conduction mechanisms in lightly-doped single-layer cuprates that exhibit both antiferromagnetic (AF) and superconducting (SC) orders simultaneously.
main_result: The high-temperature superconductivity is attributed to conduction holes hosted within a robust, strongly correlated AF ordered state of localized Cu 3d electrons.
method: The study employs multiple experimental techniques, including magnetization measurements, resistivity measurements ($ho_{\parallel}, ho_{\perp}$), and NQR spectroscopy, across varying doping levels.
model_or_system: The physical system is the lightly-doped single-layer cuprate $\mathrm{La}_2\mathrm{CuO}_{4+\delta}$ (LCO), which is studied by comparing superconducting samples ($p \approx 0.03$) to more insulating/AF samples ($p \lesssim 0.015$).
key_observables: Magnetization ($M$), electrical resistivity ($ho$), sub-lattice moments ($M_s$), AF couplings ($J_{\parallel}$), and the development of 2D AF spin correlations.
important_parameters: Doping level ($p \approx 0.03$ vs $p \lesssim 0.015$), Néel temperature ($T_N = 266 	ext{ K}$), and the superconducting critical temperature ($T_c \sim 30 	ext{ K}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the superconducting state arises from the doping of a highly localized, robust antiferromagnetically ordered background.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the temperature dependence of magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$) and magnetization ($M$) near $T_N$, and show the correlation between field-induced weak ferromagnetism transitions and sharp reductions in resistivity.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares magnetic and transport properties across different doping regimes, focusing on the anomalous behavior observed below a characteristic temperature $T^*$, and linking these anomalies to the coexistence of AF and SC orders.
why_interesting: The strong correlation between magnetism (AF order) and superconductivity in cuprates is a cornerstone problem in condensed matter physics, making this experimental work highly relevant for understanding unconventional pairing mechanisms.
